name: Tellurium
occurrence: Extremely rare in Earth's crust, recovered mainly as a by-product of copper refining.
majorUses: Solar panel material (cadmium telluride thin-film cells)
safetyNotes: Even tiny exposures cause 'tellurium breath', an intensely persistent garlic-like body odour that can last for weeks, making it one of chemistry's more socially memorable hazards.
notableCharacteristics: Named after 'tellus', Latin for Earth, as a companion name to selenium (named for the Moon).
whyHere: Sitting below selenium and sulfur, tellurium shares the -2/+4/+6 oxidation pattern of the group, but its much larger, more metallic atom gives it the thermoelectric and semiconducting behaviour that makes it valuable in solar cells.
didYouKnow: Exposure to even microgram quantities of tellurium can cause a garlicky body odour lasting weeks, produced when the body metabolizes it into a volatile methylated compound — one of the most notorious 'occupational hazard' smells in chemistry.
genZNote: Give it a breath and it'll haunt you with garlic smell for weeks. The clinginess is unmatched.
